chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man says, 'Upon me is a vow,' and he does not specify anything.' He said: 'A palmful of wheat, whether it is made hard upon him or made difficult.'
ai.seo_question: What is the default vow if a person does not specify what they vowed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a default expiation for an unspecified vow (*nadh*), prescribing a palmful of wheat (*kaffarat al-nadh*). The phrase 'ghalliza 'alayhi' indicates that the obligation is treated with strictness, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that vague vows carry a burden of certainty to ensure fulfillment. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and specificity in vows, serving as a practical guideline for believers who make general commitments to God.
